author: reek
body: read-line is two things at once: a builtin with a real emitter, and an operation declared on the Console effect. Declaring it gives it a handler-table slot, and emit-name used to consult that slot before the builtin table. No handler ever writes the slot, so the read came back zero, and zero decodes as Just "" -- an empty line, indistinguishable from a real one. Any program that cited Console read an empty line from the terminal and carried on. Dropping the cite fixed it, which is the opposite of what a cite is for.

author: reek
body: A name with a real implementation now outranks an unwritten handler slot. Inside a handle block the operation is still bound as a local, so a handler that means to override read-line still does.

author: reek
body: With no stdin this must be None, the honest end of input. It was Just "" for as long as the slot won.
